learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow for lifelong study for adequate professional development.
Know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to synthesize and concretize phenomena involving fluids and mastery of the laws governing their behavior.
Skills for solving practical engineering application cases: calculation of pipes, channels, fluid systems, etc.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics.

syllabus_topics: Continuum medium hypothesis. Density and velocity
Local thermodynamic equilibrium. Pressure, energy and equation of state.
Types of flow and movements in fluids
Material or substantial derivative. Total, local and convective acceleration.
Convective Flow and Reynolds Transport Theorem
Integral equation of momentum and angular momentum conservation
Integral equation of total and internal energy conservation
Two-dimensional flows. Couette and Poiseuille flow
Power, Specific Energies and Head Losses in Turbulence
Hydrostatic forces on flat and curved surfaces.
assessment_rules: The course offers two ordinary assessment paths: progressive and global. The progressive path combines Exam 1 (20%), Exam 2 (70%), and a Laboratory Exam (10%), with a minimum of 3.0/10.0 required for Exam 1. The global path and extraordinary call consist of a comprehensive Global Exam (90%) and the Laboratory Exam (10%). To pass, the weighted sum of all activities must be 5.0 or higher; laboratory practice is mandatory and non-recoverable.
